title: Claim and integration ledger: twisted Stieltjes calculus and harmonic Laurent identities

status_definitions.established_here_source_addition: Complete proof supplied here; the specified formulation is an addition to the inspected source set. This does not assert exhaustive global priority.
status_definitions.consolidated_existing: An established repository result or classical/literature antecedent, consolidated or applied with proof here. See the mathematical_outcome field for existing rejections.
status_definitions.correction: A confirmed source repair or an explicitly qualified editorial clarification. Patch inclusion is stated separately.
status_definitions.open: A surviving source conjecture or research target that this article does not prove.

global_qualifications: Proof status, source novelty, and global priority are distinct.
The inspected source set is specified by source_manifest.json and source_provenance.md; the audit is not exhaustive over every historical report.
Untwisted periodic/G2-style normalization is already answered by pinned continuations. The explicitly open nonintegral half-twist target is separately resolved here.
Positive beta evaluations and the classical nonsingular alternating convolution are credited antecedents.
Exact symbolic checks and numerical diagnostics corroborate the analytic proofs; numerical agreement does not prove a conjectural period relation.
No formal proof-assistant verification, numerical-period independence theorem, or S6/new-S8 resolution is claimed.

claims.title: Nonintegral Lerch finite parts and all-index multiplication
claims.statement: The retained-mode periodic family has convolution unit delta_0, explicit residues at every positive integer, cutoff-normalized Lerch jets, and a finite all-index Bell/Gamma multiplication rule. This answers the specified half-twist normalization target and extends it to every real nonintegral twist.

pinned_source_evidence.heading: Twists, characters, and alternate endpoint normalizations

claims.scope_qualification: The Lerch function, modified Stieltjes constants, and ordinary nonsingular alternating convolution are antecedents. The source addition concerns the singular distributional normalization and table; no exhaustive global priority claim is made.

claims.title: Every covariant contact correction
claims.statement: Raw finite parts and covariant derivatives differ by explicit elementary-harmonic multiples of D_theta^k delta_0; all lower ordinary delta derivatives are retained. The finite-part polygamma correction is H_k D_theta^k delta_0.

pinned_source_evidence.heading: Twists, characters, and alternate endpoint normalizations

claims.scope_qualification: D_theta=D+2*pi*i*theta acts on periodic distributions. A nonperiodic phase is used only in local or ordinary representatives, not as a global distribution multiplier.

claims.title: All-index alternating Stieltjes integral identities
claims.statement: The normalized half-twist table yields absolutely convergent subtracted integrals of modified Stieltjes functions. The wrapped integral has a negative sign, and delta_0 contributes no ordinary constant away from the endpoint.

claims.scope_qualification: The assertion is for 0<a<1; it does not assign an ordinary value to an unsubtracted divergent integral or to a coincident singularity.

claims.title: Explicit quarter-Gamma evaluation
claims.statement: At a=1/2, the fully subtracted alternating digamma integral equals pi*(4*log(Gamma(1/4))-gamma-3*log(2*pi)).

claims.scope_qualification: This is an exact consequence of the new normalized integral and classical Dirichlet beta and Gamma identities. Nielsen beta(x) and Dirichlet beta_D(s) are distinguished explicitly.

claims.title: Reflected half-twist multiplication
claims.statement: The involution J U(x)=exp(-2*pi*i*x)U(-x) reverses the half-shifted frequencies and gives the reflected generator, sample tables, and arbitrary-order polygamma contact formula.

pinned_source_evidence.heading: Twists, characters, and alternate endpoint normalizations

claims.scope_qualification: Bare reflection alone does not reverse n+1/2. The same fixed-twist involution is not asserted for arbitrary nonintegral theta.

claims.title: Unique covariant primitives and degeneration at zero twist
claims.statement: D_theta has a unique inverse on all periodic distributions. Finite Hurwitz-Lerch jet formulas give all repeated primitives, and an exact scalar zero-mode subtraction gives the untwisted Stieltjes limit with its changed convolution unit.

pinned_source_evidence.heading: Twists, characters, and alternate endpoint normalizations

claims.scope_qualification: The Gamma-ratio ordinary primitive is a classical Lerch order derivative. The statement here fixes its periodic covariant normalization and all-index zero-mode limit.

claims.title: Classical rational Lerch coordinates used in the twisted table
claims.statement: Residue-class decomposition expresses rational-twist Lerch functions in a finite colored Hurwitz sum, and therefore expresses the normalized jets in generalized Stieltjes and polygamma functions.
claims.scope_qualification: The finite Fourier decomposition and modified Stieltjes conversion are established special-function coordinates, not a new basis-independence or period-reduction claim.

claims.title: Complete principal and finite Laurent data of the outer-shift harmonic family
claims.statement: For E_r(s;a)=sum_{n>=1} e_r(n-1)/(n+a)^s, a jointly controlled Mellin continuation gives the complete principal part and finite part at s=1 and at every nonpositive integer. At s=-m the finite coefficient is [u^(r+1)] b_(m+1)(u,a)/Gamma(u-m).
claims.scope_qualification: The shift affects only the outer denominator. The full arbitrary-shift, all-depth Laurent statement was not located in the inspected source set. Young already treats unshifted height-one Laurent theory; the 2023 full text was unavailable, so global priority is not asserted. Positive spectral derivatives are outside the finite-polynomial conclusion.

claims.title: Residue term in differentiation of finite parts
claims.statement: The exact shift-derivative rule is C_(m,r) prime = m*C_(m-1,r)-R_(m-1,r), including higher-pole cases.
claims.scope_qualification: This is a necessary correction to a tempting formal manipulation. It is not an allegation that an inspected repository source makes that error.

claims.title: Reflection of finite parts mixes harmonic depths
claims.statement: The local-kernel identity phi(t,u,-1-a)=phi(-t,u,a+u) gives the exact derivative correction to ordinary Bernoulli reflection at every depth.
claims.scope_qualification: The identity is polynomial in a. Both sides represent the original shifted Dirichlet family on -1<Re(a)<0; elsewhere the polynomial finite-part continuation is meant.

claims.title: All repeated antiderivatives of harmonic finite parts
claims.statement: A finite sum of higher-m, lower-depth coefficients gives every q-fold primitive, with reciprocal-harmonic coefficients and explicit base-point normalization.
claims.scope_qualification: The usual polynomial of degree less than q is the entire integration ambiguity. These are primitives in the outer shift a, not spectral derivatives.

claims.title: Rational multiplication with finite depth corrections
claims.statement: Summing q shifted coefficient germs produces a finite exact multiplication law involving d_n^(q)(u), reciprocal-Gamma recurrences, and the necessary auxiliary A_(-1)=1/Gamma(1+u).
claims.scope_qualification: At depth zero it specializes to Hurwitz multiplication. Higher-depth correction terms are essential; the auxiliary A_(-1) is not the finite-part germ at s=1.

claims.title: Positive-integer beta evaluations and cyclotomic applications
claims.statement: The subtracted beta identity evaluates positive integer E_r(p;a) by derivatives of complete harmonic polynomials and supplies explicit cyclotomic averages and nonlinear odd-denominator examples.
claims.scope_qualification: Young 2026 includes the parametric beta-derivative baseline. The explicit applications are proved here but are not presented as a newly invented method or a proof that individual colored summands reduce to depth one.

claims.title: Untwisted periodic normalization already present in the pinned tree
claims.statement: The untwisted meromorphic Hurwitz distribution, its residue 1-delta_0 at one, its cutoff finite parts, and harmonic derivative contact terms are consolidated and independently checked.
claims.scope_qualification: An older G2-style normalization question must not be counted as newly solved at this baseline: these archived continuations already supply the untwisted answer. The nonintegral half-twist question is a separate explicit open target.

claims.title: Existing untwisted convolution algebra and ordinary realizations
claims.statement: The untwisted Bell algebra, both orientations, polygamma collapse, and low-order subtracted Stieltjes integrals are restated with complete proofs.

claims.title: Existing normalized Stieltjes primitive tower
claims.statement: The complete repeated-primitive formula and ordinary Gamma convolution are retained as a normalization foundation for the twisted extension.

claims.title: Existing reflected polylogarithm kernel and Hurwitz jet framework
claims.statement: The entire mixed-order kernel, explicit first-Stieltjes order-zero formulas, and rational-grid jet conversion are consolidated as applications of the fixed finite-part conventions.
claims.scope_qualification: The two-parameter kernel and symmetric formula already occur in the pinned reports. The individual formula is an explicit classical differentiated-Hurwitz consequence, not a global novelty claim.

claims.title: Repair the negative-real arctanh branch
claims.statement: For real theta=arcsin(lambda), the logarithm must be log(abs(tan(theta/2))); the value at lambda=0 is defined by continuity. At lambda=-1/2 the printed principal-log formula has the exact spurious term -i*pi^2/6.
claims.scope_qualification: Included in confirmed_source_corrections.patch. The article proves the repaired formula through the convergent endpoint cases; the minimal patch states -1<lambda<1.
